name: New Project
description: Creates a new project and opens the import view for selecting initial media. Start each film-of-the-project here, and keep one project per film to avoid media chaos.

name: New Sequence
description: Creates a timeline with chosen resolution, frame rate and audio track layout. Easier still: drag a clip onto the New Item button to make a sequence that matches the footage exactly.

name: Sequence Settings
description: Edits the active sequence's frame size, frame rate and preview format after creation. Check it first when renders come out the wrong shape.

name: Import
description: Brings video, image sequences, audio and graphics into the project. Import rendered archviz shots and site footage into clearly named bins from day one.

name: Media Browser
description: Browses drives and card structures with previews, importing media without leaving Premiere. Safer than Explorer for camera cards because it understands their folder formats.

name: New Bin
description: Creates a folder in the Project panel for organising clips. A disciplined bin structure — footage, renders, audio, graphics, sequences — pays off on every project.

name: Create Proxies
description: Generates lightweight copies of heavy footage that Premiere can switch to during editing, then swaps back for export. Essential for cutting 4K renders smoothly on a laptop; toggle them with the monitor's proxy button.

name: Selection Tool
description: Selects, moves and trims clips directly in the timeline. The default tool — return to it after every specialist tool so stray clicks stay harmless.

name: Track Select Forward Tool
description: Selects every clip from the click point to the end of the sequence; Shift+A selects backwards instead. Use it to shove the whole back half of an edit along when inserting a new scene.

name: Ripple Edit Tool
description: Trims a cut and automatically closes the gap, shifting everything downstream. The workhorse trimming tool — tighten shots without ever leaving black holes in the timeline.

name: Rolling Edit Tool
description: Moves the cut point between two clips without changing the overall duration — one clip gets longer, the other shorter. Perfect for retiming a cut to land on a music beat.

name: Rate Stretch Tool
description: Drags a clip's edge to change its playback speed so it fills exactly the space available. Quick for stretching a short flythrough to cover a voiceover line.

name: Razor Tool
description: Cuts a clip into two at the point you click; Shift-click cuts through all tracks. Most editors prefer Add Edit at the playhead, but the razor is direct and visual.

name: Slip Tool
description: Changes which portion of the source footage plays inside a clip without moving the clip or changing its length. Use it to catch the best moment of a camera move while keeping the cut rhythm intact.

name: Slide Tool
description: Moves a clip earlier or later in the sequence while its neighbours trim to absorb the change, keeping total duration fixed. For nudging one shot's position within a locked montage.

name: Pen Tool
description: Adds and adjusts keyframes on timeline rubber bands, such as audio volume and opacity, and draws freeform graphics. Click a clip's volume line with it to keyframe a music dip under narration.

name: Hand Tool
description: Drags the timeline view left and right without moving any clips. Middle-mouse drag does the same from any tool.

name: Zoom Tool
description: Zooms the timeline in where you click, or out with Alt held. Most editors use the plus and minus keys instead, but the tool allows marquee-zooming to an exact region.

name: Mark In
description: Sets the in point on the source monitor or sequence, defining where an edit range begins. The first half of three-point editing — mark the usable part of a shot before cutting it in.

name: Mark Out
description: Sets the out point, completing the range for an insert, overwrite or export. With in and out set on the source, one keystroke drops exactly the shot you chose into the cut.

name: Go to In / Out
menu: Markers > Go to In Point / Go to Out Point
description: Jumps the playhead straight to the marked in or out point. Keeps three-point editing entirely on the keyboard.

name: Clear In and Out
description: Removes the current in and out points in one stroke. Clear stale ranges before exporting, or you may accidentally export only a fragment.

name: Insert
description: Places the source clip at the playhead and pushes existing material later to make room. Use it when adding a shot mid-sequence without overwriting anything.

name: Overwrite
description: Places the source clip at the playhead on top of whatever is there, without shifting the sequence. The standard edit when laying shots over a locked music bed.

name: Lift
description: Removes the material between the sequence in and out points, leaving a gap. Use it when timing elsewhere must not move.

name: Extract
description: Removes the material between in and out and ripples the gap closed. The range-based sibling of ripple delete, ideal for cutting a flabby section out of a draft.

name: Add Edit
description: Cuts the clips on targeted tracks at the playhead — a keyboard razor. Add Ctrl+Shift+K to cut through every track at once.

name: Ripple Delete
menu: Right-click clip or gap > Ripple Delete
description: Deletes a clip or gap and closes the hole by pulling everything after it forward. The fastest way to keep a rough cut gapless as you strip out weak shots.

name: Snap
description: Toggles magnetic snapping of clip edges to other edits, markers and the playhead. Leave it on for assembly; flick it off for delicate frame-level nudges.

name: Add Marker
description: Drops a marker on the clip or sequence at the playhead, with optional notes and colours. Tap it on every music beat first, then cut shots to the markers.

name: Go to Next Marker
description: Jumps the playhead to the next marker; Ctrl+Shift+M goes back to the previous one. Turns beat markers into a navigation system for the whole edit.

name: Match Frame
description: Loads the source clip into the Source Monitor parked on the exact frame under the playhead. Use it to grab an alternative take or extend a shot from its original footage.

name: Select Clip at Playhead
description: Selects whatever clip sits under the playhead on targeted tracks. Combined with property shortcuts it enables rapid keyboard-only clip adjustments.

name: Ripple Trim Previous Edit
menu: Sequence > Ripple Trim Previous Edit Point to Playhead
description: Trims from the previous cut up to the playhead and ripples the sequence closed. Park the playhead where the shot should start and tap Q — brutal, fast top-trimming.

name: Ripple Trim Next Edit
menu: Sequence > Ripple Trim Next Edit Point to Playhead
description: Trims from the playhead forward to the next cut and closes the gap. The tail-trimming twin of Q — together they make rough cuts astonishingly quick.

name: Extend Selected Edit
menu: Sequence > Extend Selected Edit to Playhead
description: Rolls the selected edit point to the playhead position, lengthening one clip and shortening its neighbour. Select a cut, park the playhead on the beat, press E.

name: Toggle Trim Type
menu: Double-click an edit point to enter trim mode; Shift+T cycles trim type
description: Cycles the selected edit point between regular, ripple and rolling trims, shown by red or yellow brackets. Double-clicking a cut opens the dedicated trim view for refining it while looping playback.

name: Speed/Duration
description: Sets a clip's playback speed by percentage or target duration, with reverse and frame-blending options. Slow a 50 fps site clip to 50 percent for smooth half-speed motion.

name: Time Remapping
menu: Clip > Show Clip Keyframes > Time Remapping > Speed
description: Keyframes a clip's speed over time directly on the timeline rubber band, allowing ramps between fast and slow. Use it to glide quickly through a corridor then linger in the main space.

name: Nest
description: Collapses selected clips into a single nested sequence that can be trimmed and effected as one. Nest a finished montage section before applying a unified grade or transition.

name: Group
description: Links selected clips so they select and move together, without creating a new sequence. Lighter-weight than nesting for keeping a title and its backing plate in sync.

name: Ungroup
description: Releases grouped clips back to independent selection. Necessary before trimming one member differently from the rest.

name: Link / Unlink
description: Joins or separates a clip's video and audio so they move together or independently. Unlink to delete scratch audio from renders, or to slip sound against picture for a J-cut.

name: Enable Clip
description: Toggles a clip on or off without deleting it — disabled clips render black and silent. Useful for comparing versions of a shot or muting an overlay during review.

name: Label Colours
description: Assigns colours to clips in the project and timeline. Colour-code by content — renders, drone footage, graphics, audio — so the timeline reads at a glance.

name: Replace with Clip
menu: Right-click timeline clip > Replace With Clip > From Source Monitor
description: Swaps a timeline clip for the Source Monitor clip while keeping its position, duration and applied effects. Ideal for dropping in an updated render over an old placeholder version.

name: Synchronise Clips
description: Aligns selected clips by their audio waveforms or timecode. The rescue for interview or walkthrough footage where camera audio and a separate recorder must line up.

name: Merge Clips
description: Combines a video clip with separately recorded audio into a single new clip for editing. Merge once in the project so every future cut uses the good sound automatically.

name: Paste Attributes
description: Pastes chosen properties — motion, opacity, effects, colour — from a copied clip onto others. Grade one shot, then paste its Lumetri settings across the whole scene.

name: Audio Gain
description: Adjusts a clip's audio level before it reaches the mixer, with a normalise option to a target loudness. Set music and voiceover gains here first, then fine-tune with keyframes.

name: Audio Track Mixer
description: A mixing-desk view with faders, pans and effects per track rather than per clip. Balance the music, ambience and narration tracks of a film here as a whole.

name: Essential Sound Panel
description: Tags audio as dialogue, music, SFX or ambience and offers plain-language tools — loudness matching, ducking, repair. Auto-ducking music under a voiceover takes seconds here.

name: Mute / Solo Track
menu: Timeline track header M and S buttons
description: Silences a track (M) or isolates it (S) during playback. Solo the narration to check clarity, mute the music to hear what the ambience is really doing.

name: Show Audio Waveforms
menu: Timeline wrench menu > Show Audio Waveform
description: Displays waveforms on audio clips in the timeline. Expand the music track's height and cut visually to the drum hits.

name: Effect Controls Panel
description: Edits the selected clip's built-in motion, opacity and speed properties plus any applied effects, with keyframing. Where you scale a render to punch in, or keyframe a slow push on a still.

name: Effects Panel
description: Searches all video and audio effects and transitions for dragging onto clips. Type-search it rather than browsing — the folder tree is deep.

name: Apply Video Transition
description: Adds the default transition — normally a cross dissolve — to the selected edit points. Set your preferred duration in preferences, and resist using anything fancier without a reason.

name: Apply Audio Transition
description: Adds the default constant-power crossfade to selected audio edits. A short crossfade on every music and ambience cut removes clicks and bumps instantly.

name: Lumetri Colour Panel
description: The main grading interface — basic correction, creative LUTs, curves, colour wheels, HSL secondaries and vignette. Grade shot-matched sections on adjustment layers to keep the film's look coherent.

name: Lumetri Scopes
description: Displays waveform, vectorscope and histogram readouts of the programme image. Trust the scopes over your monitor when checking exposure and skin tones for delivery.

name: Adjustment Layer
description: Creates a transparent layer whose effects apply to every track beneath it. Lay one across a scene and grade it once instead of clip by clip.

name: Warp Stabiliser
menu: Effects > Video Effects > Distort > Warp Stabilizer
description: Analyses and smooths shaky footage directly in the timeline. Apply it to handheld site walkthroughs; use Smooth Motion rather than No Motion to keep some life in the shot.

name: Masking and Tracking
menu: Effect Controls > effect mask (ellipse, rectangle, pen) + tracker
description: Draws a mask on any effect so it applies only inside the shape, then tracks the mask to follow movement through the shot. Use it to brighten just the building facade or blur a passer-by's face.

name: Essential Graphics Panel
description: Builds and edits titles, shapes and layered graphics, and browses installed Motion Graphics templates. Design a consistent lower-third for project captions once and reuse it throughout.

name: Type Tool
description: Creates text directly in the Programme Monitor as a graphic clip on the timeline. Fine for quick captions; style the result properly in the Essential Graphics panel.

name: Install Motion Graphics Template
menu: Graphics and Titles > Install Motion Graphics Template (.mogrt)
description: Adds a .mogrt file — often built in After Effects — to the Essential Graphics library for drag-and-drop use. Package your studio's animated titles as MOGRTs so every film shares the same identity.

name: Export
description: Opens the export view for choosing format, preset, range and destination. H.264 with a high-bitrate preset covers most client review and web delivery needs.

name: Export In to Out Range
description: Exports only the section between the sequence in and out points. Perfect for sending a single revised scene rather than re-rendering the whole film.

name: Send to Media Encoder Queue
menu: Export view > Send to Media Encoder
description: Queues the export in Adobe Media Encoder so rendering happens in the background. Stack multiple formats — a 4K master and a compressed review copy — and keep editing meanwhile.

name: Render In to Out
description: Pre-renders the effects-heavy sections of the marked range so the timeline plays back smoothly, turning the render bar green. Do it before client playback sessions to avoid stutters.

name: Play/Stop
description: Starts and stops playback in the active monitor. The most-pressed key in editing; pair it with JKL for speed control.

name: JKL Playback
description: Shuttle controls: L plays forward and speeds up on repeat presses, J does the same in reverse, K pauses. The professional way to scrub footage while logging site material.

name: Play Around
description: Plays a few seconds either side of the playhead and stops. The quickest way to judge a trim in context without manually rewinding.

name: Step One Frame
description: Nudges the playhead a single frame backwards or forwards; Shift+arrow jumps five frames. Frame-stepping is how you find the exact cut point on a beat.

name: Go to Next Edit Point
description: Jumps the playhead to the next or previous cut on targeted tracks. Combined with Q, W and E it makes trimming an entirely keyboard-driven rhythm.

name: Toggle Full Screen
menu: Ctrl+` toggles full-screen playback of the active monitor
description: Expands the active monitor to fill the screen for distraction-free review. Use it when showing a work-in-progress cut to colleagues at your desk.

name: Maximise Frame
menu: Press ` with the pointer over a panel
description: Temporarily expands the panel under the cursor to fill the workspace; press again to restore. Maximise the timeline for complex multi-track passages, then pop back.

name: Zoom Timeline In / Out
description: Zooms the timeline view in and out around the playhead. Zoom in for frame-accurate trims, out for judging overall pacing.

name: Zoom to Sequence
description: Fits the entire sequence into the timeline window. Tap it whenever you are lost deep in a zoomed view.

name: Project Panel
description: Focuses the Project panel, home of all bins, clips and sequences. Keyboard panel-switching (Shift+1 to Shift+9) keeps hands off the mouse during assembly.

name: Source Monitor
description: Focuses the Source Monitor, where raw clips are reviewed and marked before editing into the sequence. Load, mark in and out, then insert or overwrite — the classic loop.

name: Timeline Panel
description: Focuses the timeline, where the film is actually built. Panel focus matters — many shortcuts act on whichever panel is active.

name: Programme Monitor
description: Focuses the Programme Monitor, showing the sequence at the playhead. Its safe margins, playback resolution and comparison view all live in its settings menu.

name: Deselect All
description: Clears the current selection in the active panel. Worth internalising because several commands behave differently when clips are selected versus not.
